A 2x2 Landbound minion stays enabled when Flood covers only part of its footprint, because any remaining occupied land location keeps Landbound satisfied.
A 2x2 Landbound minion becomes Disabled in place when Flood covers every occupied cell of its footprint.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion stays enabled when Drought covers only part of its footprint, because any remaining occupied Water location keeps Waterbound satisfied.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion becomes Disabled in place when Drought covers every occupied cell of its footprint.
A 2x2 Landbound minion is Disabled on an all-Water footprint and becomes enabled in place when Drought covers every occupied cell, because Drought makes those sites land again.
A 2x2 Waterbound minion is Disabled on an all-land footprint and becomes enabled in place when Flood covers every occupied cell, because Flood makes those sites Water.

Magic that gains control of a target enemy minion this turn may choose a distant enemy, transfers control without changing ownership, and untaps that minion so its new controller can use it immediately.
Temporary enemy-minion control expires at the current End Phase and restores the previous controller without changing ownership.
Magic that gains control of a target enemy minion until it loses Stealth may choose a distant enemy, transfers control without changing ownership, grants Stealth, and taps that minion.
Stealth-bound enemy-minion control survives the current End Phase and restores the previous controller when the stolen minion loses Stealth, without changing ownership.

Minion Genesis that gains control of tapped minions here until this leaves steals each tapped minion sharing its footprint without targeting, leaves Ward intact, skips untapped and distant minions, and keeps control through the current End Phase.
Source-bound Genesis control restores the previous controller when the source leaves play, without changing ownership.

A carried Artifact that is sacrificed to steal a target enemy minion here grants its bearer control of that minion until the bearer leaves, offers only unstealthed enemy minions sharing the bearer's footprint, and leaves ownership unchanged.
Sacrifice-to-steal Artifact control survives the current End Phase and restores the previous controller when the bearer leaves play, without changing ownership.

A minion that lets nearby Avatars discard a card to gain control of it offers that paid steal only to a nearby Avatar, transfers control without targeting so Ward does not absorb, and leaves ownership unchanged.
Nearby-Avatar discard control is permanent: it survives End Phase, does not revert when the source stays in play, and is not offered to a distant Avatar.

Genesis that lets the previous player control each player during their next turn schedules that swap immediately, then the previous player submits the opponent's next turn, sees that player's hidden hand, and spends that player's resources while the controlled player cannot act.
Previous-player turn control applies to each player's next turn once, then expires: after both scheduled turns resolve, each player submits their own decisions again.

Magic that draws a site and then may play a land site draws one hidden Atlas card, then offers an extra play of a printed land site plus a decline. The extra play is legal while the Avatar is already tapped and does not tap the Avatar. Printed water sites are not offered.

Magic that draws a site and then may play a water site offers only printed water sites after the draw. Declining leaves the drawn water site in hand and returns to the main phase without tapping the Avatar.

Magic that disables a minion within two measured steps until damaged offers only same-region minions at the caster's occupied cells or a cardinal walk of at most two steps. Avatars and a minion three steps away are not offered. The chosen minion becomes Disabled until it takes damage, cannot use printed abilities, and wakes after positive damage.

Enemy Ward absorbs measured disable-until-damaged Magic and breaks without applying the disable. A successful disable lasts through the caster's next Start Phase instead of expiring like Freeze, and stays until the minion takes damage.

Magic that grants an allied minion +2 power this turn and then draws a spell offers only allied minions, never an Avatar or an enemy. The power uses the shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. The power expires at End Phase.
Grant-+2-this-turn then draw-spell Magic applies the power first. If the caster's Spellbook is empty, the required draw ends the game as a deck-out without a spell-drawn event.

Magic that grants an allied minion Lethal this turn and then draws a spell offers only allied minions, never an Avatar or an enemy. The Lethal mark uses the shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. Lethal expires at End Phase.
After grant-Lethal-this-turn then draw-spell Magic resolves, one point of damage from that minion destroys a tougher minion. The same strike without the grant only wounds it.

Magic that grants an allied minion Airborne this turn and then draws a spell offers only allied minions, never an Avatar or an enemy. The Airborne mark uses the shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. Airborne expires at End Phase.
A grounded minion cannot strike an Airborne enemy. After grant-Airborne-this-turn then draw-spell Magic resolves, that same minion can strike the Airborne enemy.

Magic that grants an ally +1 movement this turn and then draws a spell offers allied Avatars and minions, never an enemy. The movement mark uses a shared this-turn source list. The drawn spell stays hidden from the opponent. The movement expires at End Phase.

A minion with no printed movement bonus can reach an adjacent cell but not a cell two steps away. After grant-+1-movement-this-turn then draw-spell Magic resolves, that same minion can reach the two-step cell.
Genesis that untaps adjacent allies untaps a tapped Avatar on a bordering cell in the same region. An enemy minion two steps away is not untapped.
Genesis that untaps adjacent allies does not untap a tapped Avatar sharing the newcomer's cell. Same-cell is not adjacent.
Grant-Stealth-to-allied-minions then draw-spell Magic stealths every allied minion, never the Avatar or an enemy, and then draws one hidden spell.
Grant-Stealth-to-allied-minions then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no allied minion is in play. No minion is stealthed.

Grant-Stealth-to-an-allied-minion occupying an enemy site then draw-spell Magic offers only an allied minion standing on an enemy-controlled site, stealths that minion, and then draws one hidden spell. Allies on friendly sites, Avatars, and enemy minions are not offered.
Grant-Stealth-to-an-allied-minion occupying an enemy site then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no allied minion occupies an enemy site. A home-site ally is not stealthed.
Summon-token-to-allied-minion then draw-spell Magic summons one source-linked token onto an allied minion's surface cell and then draws one hidden spell. Avatars and enemy minions are not hosts.
Summon-token-to-allied-minion then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no allied minion is in play. No token is summoned.
Ward-each-allied-minion-at-target-water-site Magic offers only Water sites, Wards every allied minion occupying the chosen site, and leaves an enemy minion there unwarded.
Ward-each-allied-minion-at-target-water-site Magic does not offer an Earth site. Targeting a Water site with no allied minion is a paid no-op.

Pull-adjacent-aboveground-unit-to-target-water-site then draw-spell Magic offers a Water site and an aboveground unit bordering that site, pulls that unit onto the site, and then draws one hidden spell. A unit occupying the site is not adjacent. Earth sites are not offered.
Pull-adjacent-aboveground-unit-to-target-water-site then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no aboveground unit borders a Water site. No unit is moved.

Return-up-to-three-cemetery-cards-to-deck-bottom then draw-spell Magic offers each subset of up to three own-cemetery cards, returns the chosen cards to the bottoms of their owners' matching decks in instance-id order, and then draws one hidden spell.
Return-up-to-three-cemetery-cards-to-deck-bottom then draw-spell Magic still draws one hidden spell when no cemetery card is returned. The just-cast Magic stays in the cemetery.

Ward-nearby-minion-or-site Magic offers each nearby minion and each nearby site, including an enemy minion on the caster's cell. A far site is not offered. Choosing a minion applies the shared Ward mark.
Ward-nearby-minion-or-site Magic can Ward a nearby site. The next targeted destroy consumes that one-shot mark, leaves the site in play, and then a second destroy removes it.

Silence-and-tap-nearby-minion then may-draw-spell Magic offers each nearby minion with or without a spell draw. Choosing the draw Silences and taps that minion, then draws one hidden spell. A far minion is not offered. Silence is this-turn ability loss, not Disable, so a printed Spellcaster cannot cast while Silenced while the Avatar still can.
Silence-and-tap-nearby-minion then may-draw-spell Magic still Silences and taps when the spell draw is declined. Silence expires at End Phase; the tap remains.

Ally-submerges-target-nearby-minion Magic offers each controlled ally paired with each other minion nearby that ally, including an enemy on the ally's cell. A far minion is not offered. Choosing an ally and a nearby minion on a Water site submerges that minion.
Ally-submerges-target-nearby-minion Magic still offers a nearby pair on an Earth site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underwater layer exists.

Ally-strikes-each-enemy-at-its-location Magic offers each controlled ally and makes that ally strike every enemy sharing its current cell and region. A far enemy is not struck. The ally does not step.
Ally-strikes-each-enemy-at-its-location Magic still offers each controlled ally when no enemy shares that location, then resolves as a paid no-op without a strike.

Burrow-target-adjacent-minion Magic offers only a minion that borders the caster. A same-cell minion and a far minion are not offered. Choosing an adjacent minion on an Earth site burrows that minion.
Burrow-target-adjacent-minion Magic still offers an adjacent minion on a Water site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists.

Ally-takes-up-to-two-steps Magic offers each controlled ally paired with each card-effect destination within two cardinal steps. After C4, C3, and C2 exist, an ally at C4 is offered C2, C3, and C4, not C1. Casting to C2 emits a two-step unit-stepped event.
Ally-takes-up-to-two-steps Magic still offers the ally's current cell. Choosing to stay resolves as a paid no-op without a unit-stepped event.

Teleport-target-minion-artifact-or-aura-one-diagonal Magic offers a minion paired with an existing diagonal location. After C4, D4, and D3 exist, a minion at C4 is offered D3 only. Casting teleports that minion to D3 without a step.
Teleport-target-minion-artifact-or-aura-one-diagonal Magic offers no cast when the only extra site is cardinal. A minion at C4 with C3 present cannot be teleported.

Grant-double-damage-to-ally-next-strike-this-turn Magic marks a chosen ally. That ally's next unit strike this turn deals double damage, so an attack-2 minion kills a defense-3 enemy that it would only wound without the grant.
The next-strike-double mark expires at End Phase. A later strike uses the ally's printed attack and only wounds the same tougher enemy.

Kill-mortal-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic offers the same measured locations as area damage: existing sites within two cardinal steps of the caster footprint. Casting at a shared site kills every Mortal minion there, leaves a non-Mortal occupant unwounded, and does not kill a Mortal three cardinal steps away.

Kill-mortal-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location that holds only a non-Mortal minion. Casting there is a paid no-op: the non-Mortal stays unwounded and the spell still resolves.

Destroy-artifacts-and-auras-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic offers locations within two measured steps of the caster. After C4 and C3 exist, choosing C3 destroys a loose Artifact there and leaves a far Artifact at C1, which is three steps away and not offered.
Destroy-artifacts-and-auras-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location with no Artifact or Aura. Choosing that location resolves as a paid no-op.

Destroy-minions-at-water-site-within-two-steps Magic offers only Water sites within two measured cardinal steps of the caster footprint. Casting at C4 kills every minion occupying that Water site, including a non-Mortal, and leaves a Mortal three cardinal steps away at C1. An Earth site at C3 is not offered.
Destroy-minions-at-water-site-within-two-steps Magic still offers an empty Water site. Casting there is a paid no-op: the spell still resolves.

Banish-demon-and-undead-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic offers the same measured locations as Mortality: existing sites within two cardinal steps of the caster footprint. Casting at a shared site banishes every Demon or Undead minion there, leaves a living non-Demon non-Undead occupant untouched, and does not offer or banish an Undead three cardinal steps away.

Banish-demon-and-undead-minions-at-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location that holds only a non-Demon non-Undead minion. Casting there is a paid no-op: the occupant stays and the spell still resolves.

Destroy-undead-minions-and-artifacts-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic offers locations within two measured steps of the caster. After C4 and C3 exist, choosing C3 kills an Undead minion and destroys a loose Artifact there, and leaves a non-Undead beast at C4 unwounded.
Destroy-undead-minions-and-artifacts-at-a-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers a location with no Undead minion or Artifact. Choosing that location resolves as a paid no-op.

Destroy-own-artifact-at-location-for-area-damage Magic offers a controlled loose or carried Artifact paired with its location. After a relic sits at C3 with an enemy minion there, casting destroys that relic and deals 3 damage to each other Unit at C3.
Destroy-own-artifact-at-location-for-area-damage Magic is unoffered when the caster controls no Artifact, even if an enemy Artifact is in play.

Summon-token-to-each-controlled-site-bordering-enemy-site Magic places one source-linked token on every controlled site that borders an enemy-controlled site, in stable cell order. After North controls C4, C3, C1 and South controls B2 with a minion there, casting summons foot-soldier tokens onto B3 and C3.

Summon-token-to-each-controlled-site-bordering-enemy-site Magic still resolves when no controlled site borders an enemy site. Casting with only C4 in play is a paid no-op: no tokens appear and the spell still resolves.

Disable-target-nearby-minion-until-next-turn Magic offers a minion within nearby range of the caster footprint. Casting disables that minion until the caster's next Start Phase, blocking its actions while disabled, then the flag expires on that boundary.
Disable-target-nearby-minion-until-next-turn Magic does not offer a minion three measured cardinal steps away from the caster footprint, even when a closer minion is legal.

Summon-random-minion-from-any-cemetery Magic selects one random minion from either cemetery, then offers free placement onto a legal site. After a minion dies to the cemetery, casting Raise Dead returns that minion to C4 at zero mana.
Summon-random-minion-from-any-cemetery Magic still resolves when both cemeteries hold no minions. Casting with empty cemeteries is a paid no-op: magic-cast and magic-resolved only.
Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic burrows a chosen minion on an Earth site. After a Burrowing minion occupies C1, casting moves that minion underground and it stays in play.
Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic still offers a minion on a Water site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists. The minion stays on the surface unchanged.

Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic burrows every surface minion at the chosen land site in canonical instance-id order. After two Burrowing minions occupy C1, casting at that site moves both underground and they stay in play.
Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic does not offer a water-only site, because no Underground layer exists there. An Earth site remains offered.

Damage-each-unit-at-location-within-two-steps Magic offers existing locations within two measured cardinal steps of the caster footprint. After C4 and C3 exist, choosing C3 deals 3 damage to each Unit there: an unwarded minion takes 3, Ward absorbs for a second minion, and Avatars at C4 and C1 stay unwounded. Location offers are not unit targets, so Stealth does not filter them.
Damage-each-unit-at-location-within-two-steps Magic still offers an empty measured location. Casting at empty C3 is a paid no-op: magic-cast and magic-resolved only.

Submerge-target-minion Magic offers a same-region minion at a Water site and forcefully submerges a Submerge minion there. After south summons at C1 on a Water site, casting Drown moves the minion underwater and keeps it in play.
Submerge-target-minion Magic at an earth-only site resolves as a paid no-op because no underwater layer exists there.
Return-minion-from-own-cemetery Magic offers only the caster's own cemetery minions and returns the chosen instance to the hidden Spellbook hand with source-linked evidence.
Return-minion-from-own-cemetery Magic with an empty own cemetery still resolves as a paid no-op.
Damage-target-unit Magic offers same-region minions and deals lethal damage through the shared death pipeline when defense is exceeded.
Damage-target-unit Magic lets enemy Ward absorb the complete damage event and break without dealing damage.
Grant-charge-to-ally-this-turn Magic offers controlled allies, grants temporary Charge, and lets a newly summoned sick minion Move and Attack immediately.
Grant-charge-to-ally-this-turn Magic still offers the caster's Avatar when no allied minion is in play and grants Charge through resolution.
Leap-attack-ally Magic optionally steps a controlled ally before striking every enemy at the destination cell.
Leap-attack-ally Magic lets an immobile ally only stay and strike at its current location without stepping.
Lure-enemy-minion-one-step-closer Magic tempts a nearby enemy minion to take its own closer step toward the caster's ally.
Lure-enemy-minion-one-step-closer Magic still resolves as a paid no-op when no nearby enemy minion qualifies.
Fight-ally-with-adjacent-enemy Magic makes a chosen ally fight a targeted adjacent enemy through the shared fight pipeline.
Fight-ally-with-adjacent-enemy Magic breaks Ward on the target without entering combat.
Damage-each-aboveground-minion Magic simultaneously damages every aboveground minion.
Damage-each-aboveground-minion Magic lets Ward absorb the damage on a surviving minion.
Damage-random-unit-at-location Magic targets a surface location and deterministically damages one random unit there.
Damage-random-unit-at-location Magic lets Ward absorb the random hit without dealing damage.
Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic kills only a wounded minion in the caster region.
Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic offers no target when every minion in the caster region is healthy.
Tap-target-minion Magic exhausts a ready same-region minion.
Tap-target-minion Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and no tap event is emitted.
Untap-target-minion Magic readies a tapped same-region minion without breaking Ward.
Untap-target-minion Magic that targets an already-untapped minion is a paid no-op.
Grant-Ward Magic marks an unwarded same-region minion without breaking an existing mark.
Grant-Ward Magic that targets an already-warded minion is a paid no-op.
Grant-Stealth Magic hides an enemy minion from later targeting.
Grant-Stealth Magic does not offer an already-stealthed enemy minion.
Kill-target-minion Magic destroys a healthy same-region minion and never offers an Avatar.
Kill-target-minion Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and the minion survives.
Bounce Magic returns a healthy same-region minion to its owner's hand and never offers an Avatar.
Bounce Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and the minion stays on the board.

Destroy-site Magic offers every real site including the caster's own, never offers Rubble or a void, replaces the chosen site with Rubble, and moves that site into its owner's cemetery. Occupants remain on the Rubble.
Destroy-site Magic that would destroy a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site in play, and still resolves.
Return-site Magic returns a real site to its owner's Atlas hand, leaves no Rubble, and banishes surface minions occupying it. Avatars remain at the emptied cell.
Return-site Magic that would return a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site and its occupants in play, and still resolves.

Mill-spell Magic offers only both Avatars, never a minion, and puts the printed number of the chosen player's top Spellbook cards into that owner's cemetery in deck order. Identities are public. The game stays active when cards remain.
Mill-spell Magic that finds an empty Spellbook is a paid no-op. It does not draw, does not lose to deck-out, and emits no discard events.
Mill-site Magic is the Atlas sibling of mill-spell Magic: it offers only both Avatars and puts top Atlas cards into the owner's cemetery in deck order without drawing or decking.
Mill-site Magic that finds an empty Atlas is a paid no-op. It does not draw, does not lose to deck-out, and emits no discard events.
Return-artifact Magic detaches a carried Artifact and returns it to its owner's Spellbook hand. The opponent sees only the resulting hand count, and the Artifact does not enter a cemetery.
Return-artifact Magic offers no target when no Artifact occupies the caster region, including when only a minion is in play.

Destroy-artifact Magic offers every Artifact in the caster region whether loose or carried, moves a real Artifact into its owner's cemetery, and leaves no later Artifact target once the realm is empty of them.
Destroy-artifact Magic offers no target when no Artifact occupies the caster region, including when only a minion is in play.

Cemetery Magic return is the Rescue sibling for Magic cards: it offers only Magic in the caster's own cemetery, never a minion, site, artifact, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.
Cemetery Magic return that finds no Magic in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Artifact return is the Rescue sibling for Artifacts: it offers only Artifacts in the caster's own cemetery, never a Magic card, minion, site, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.

Cemetery Artifact return that finds no Artifact in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Site return is the Rescue sibling for Sites: it offers only Sites in the caster's own cemetery, never Magic already there, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Atlas hand rather than the Spellbook.

Cemetery Site return that finds no Site in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Cemetery Aura return is the Rescue sibling for Auras: it offers only Auras in the caster's own cemetery, never a Magic card, minion, site, artifact, or an opponent's cemetery card, and returns the unchanged instance to the hidden Spellbook hand.

Cemetery Aura return that finds no Aura in the caster's own cemetery is a paid no-choice resolution, even when the cemetery holds Magic. It still pays and enters the cemetery, and emits no return event.

Target-player discard Magic offers only both Avatars. After the cast is announced, the targeted player chooses one of their own Atlas or Spellbook hand cards. The choice is a pending Storyline that transfers the decision seat; the caster cannot pick the card, and opponent hand identities stay redacted until the discard is public in the cemetery.
The same targeted discard is a paid no-op when the chosen player has no hand cards. It never becomes a random discard and never decks out.
Targetless draw-spell Magic pays its cost, draws the printed number of hidden Spellbook cards in deck order, and enters its owner's cemetery. The opponent sees only the new hand count.
Targetless draw-spell Magic draws every remaining Spellbook card it can, then loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library.
Targetless draw-site Magic pays its cost, draws the printed number of hidden Atlas cards in deck order, and enters its owner's cemetery. The opponent sees only the new Atlas hand count.
Targetless draw-site Magic draws every remaining Atlas card it can, then loses immediately when a required draw finds an empty library.
Target-player life-loss Magic pays its cost, offers only both Avatars, never offers a minion, and reduces the chosen Avatar's life without dealing damage. The loss is not a death blow.
Target-player life-loss Magic that reduces an Avatar to zero life reaches Death's Door without ending the game. Further life loss against that Avatar is a no-op and is never a death blow.

Target-player life-gain Magic pays its cost, offers only both Avatars, never offers a minion, and heals the chosen Avatar through the shared printed-life cap. Unlike controller-only healing, it can restore an opponent.
Target-player life-gain Magic that would heal an Avatar at Death's Door is a paid no-op. Life stays at zero, the game stays active, and no healing event is emitted.

A player-chosen additional discard cost is a Storyline choice among every other hand card. It cannot select the spell being cast, pays into the owner's cemetery before the cast is announced, and then the companion effect resolves.

The same additional discard cost issues no cast when the caster has no other hand card. Remaining copies of the spell still count as other hand cards; an empty Atlas and a singleton Spellbook leave the spell unoffered.

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic burrows a chosen ordinary minion on an Earth site. The minion has no Burrowing, so region settlement kills it immediately after the burrow and it goes to its owner's cemetery.
Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic still offers an ordinary minion on a Water site, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists. The minion stays on the surface unchanged.

Craterize-style Magic pays an Atlas discard, destroys an unprotected site into Rubble, and deals its printed grid damage to the occupant. Plain destroy-site Magic (0623) creates Rubble without dealing damage.

Craterize-style Magic that would destroy a site that cannot be moved, destroyed, or modified is prevented, leaves the site in play, still pays the Atlas discard, still deals its grid damage to the occupant, and still resolves. Plain destroy-site protection (0624) has no damage companion.

Nearby-control Magic transfers a minion and its Deathrite to the new controller. Targeted Magic is a non-unit source: killing the stolen minion draws a site for the thief, and the corpse still enters the owner's cemetery.
Nearby-control Magic does not offer a far minion. Targeted Magic still kills that minion as a non-unit source and resolves Deathrite for the original controller.

Freeze Magic that disables a nearby minion until the caster's next Start Phase offers a same-region minion occupying the caster footprint. Casting disables that minion, blocking its actions until the flag expires on that turn boundary.
Freeze Magic that targets an enemy warded minion is absorbed. Ward breaks and the minion is not Disabled.
Heal-target-minion Magic removes damage from a living minion in the same turn it was wounded. Avatars are not legal targets. The heal does not kill the minion.
Heal-target-minion Magic offers only minions. A Death's Door Avatar is never a legal target. Healing an undamaged minion is a paid no-op: no heal event is emitted and the minion stays at zero damage.
Magic can grant Airborne to a controlled ally for the current turn. The grant is recorded on minions as a temporary source, and public observations show the minion as Airborne.
Grant-Airborne Magic still records a temporary source on a minion that is already Airborne. Shared End Phase cleanup expires that source, and printed Airborne remains.

Destroy-aura Magic offers every realm Aura, moves a real Aura into its owner's cemetery, and leaves no later Aura target once the realm is empty of them. The event is aura-destroyed rather than a return to hand or a duration dispel.
Destroy-aura Magic offers no target when no Aura occupies the realm, including when only a minion is in play.

Return-target-aura Magic returns a realm Flood to its owner's Spellbook hand. The Aura leaves the realm, Flood water leaves the covered sites, the opponent sees only the updated hand count, and the targeting key is the realm Aura rather than a cemetery card.
Return-target-aura Magic offers no target when no Aura occupies the realm, including when only a minion is in play. A minion is not a realm Aura, so the bounce spell stays in hand.

The same additional discard cost may take an Atlas card instead of a spell. Paying that Atlas identity puts the site in the owner's cemetery before the cast is announced, then the companion effect resolves.

Every issued chosen-discard cast includes the chosen identity; there is no no-choice cast while another hand card remains. Atlas leftovers still pay after other spells are gone, and the spell being cast is never a legal discard.

Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic kills a wounded minion in the caster region and does not offer a wounded minion in a different region. After two surface minions are wounded, burrowing one underground leaves only the surface copy as a legal Fatality target. Distinct from 0609, which never places a wounded minion off the caster's region.

Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic offers no target when the only wounded minion occupies a different region from the caster. A wounded underground minion is excluded even though that same minion was a legal surface target before it was burrowed. Distinct from 0610, which proves the all-healthy surface case.

Genesis strike-each-enemy-here hits every enemy sharing the newcomer's cell, including the Avatar standing on its own site. Co-located allies and the striker are skipped. Ward absorbs a strike without dealing damage.

Genesis strike-each-enemy-here does not strike co-located allies or the striker, and it does not reach enemies occupying a different cell. Summoning onto the controller's own site emits no strike when every enemy is elsewhere.

Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic burrows a loose Artifact at the chosen land site. After an uncarried Artifact occupies C1, casting at that site moves the Artifact underground in place. This is distinct from minion-only Cave-In (0587) and from targeted Bury (0043).

Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic detaches an Avatar-carried Artifact at the chosen land site and burrows it independently. The Avatar stays on the surface. A minion-only Cave-In (0587) has no Artifact to detach.

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic burrows a chosen loose Artifact on an Earth site. After an uncarried Artifact occupies C1, casting moves that Artifact underground in place. This is distinct from ordinary-minion Bury death (0655) and from area Cave-In Artifact occupancy (0677).

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic detaches an Avatar-carried Artifact and burrows it independently. The Avatar stays on the surface. Ordinary-minion Bury (0655) has no Artifact to detach, and area Cave-In (0678) targets the land site rather than the Artifact.

Return-minion-from-own-cemetery Magic offers only the caster's own cemetery minion when an opposing cemetery minion is also present, and returns the chosen instance to the hidden Spellbook hand. Distinct from 0593, which never places an opposing cemetery minion.

Return-minion-from-own-cemetery Magic with an empty own cemetery still resolves as a paid no-op when the opponent's cemetery holds a minion. The opposing minion is not offered. Distinct from 0594, which has no cemetery minions at all.

Nearby-control Magic, after the caster Avatar steps from C4 to C3, offers the adjacent C2 minion and transfers it and its Deathrite to the caster. The two-step C1 minion stays unoffered on that same board. Distinct from 0659, which steals a same-cell minion with no far candidate present.

Nearby-control Magic, after the caster Avatar steps from C4 to C3, does not offer the two-step C1 minion even while the adjacent C2 minion is a legal target. Killing that far minion resolves Deathrite for the original controller. Distinct from 0660, which places only a far minion three steps from an unmoved caster.

Targeted Magic is a non-unit source: it offers Avatars and a same-region minion, then kills a Deathrite minion that prevents damage from units of power 4 or more. The spell identity is the damage source, Deathrite draws a site for the controller, and both the corpse and the spell enter their owners' cemeteries. Distinct from 0595, which has no Deathrite, and from 0660, which proves Deathrite after Mesmerism fails.

Targeted Magic can damage an Avatar. A 1-life Avatar reaches Death's Door without ending the game; a later-turn Magic hit is a death blow and finishes the match with avatar_defeated. Distinct from 0650, which uses target-player life-loss rather than damageTargetUnit.

Token Magic summons source-linked tokens in stable cell order. After North controls C4, C3, and B3 and South occupies B2, casting places foot-soldier tokens on B3 then C3. Each identity is hashed from card, cell, ordinal, owner, token source, spell instance, and pre-cast state version, and the receipt has no random draws. Distinct from 0579, which proves bordering-site occupancy without the identity recipe or empty random-draw proof.

A Magic-summoned 1x1 token that dies in combat is banished instead of entering a cemetery: the fight emits minion-died then minion-banished, and the token instance is absent from its owner's cemetery. Distinct from 0372, which proves the same exit for a 2x2 Genesis token.

A printed Spellcaster may cast Magic and summon on the turn it enters, even while summoning sick. Freeze on itself reveals Stealth and Disables the caster. The same sick caster can summon a Waterbound Spellcaster onto land; that summoned minion is Disabled and cannot cast or summon. Distinct from 0151, which grants Spellcaster from a Tower rather than the printed fact.

A printed Spellcaster may still cast after tapping for mana. Freeze originates at the caster's site, so a tapped minion at C3 can Disable a nearby C2 minion while the Avatar at C4 cannot. Distinct from 0151 (Tower-granted Spellcaster) and from 0661 (Freeze itself).

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic immediately settles a chosen Deathrite minion on an Earth site. The minion has no Burrowing, so the same receipt burrows it, draws a site for its controller, and kills it. The game stays in main; there is no Deathrite-order prompt. Distinct from ordinary-minion Bury death (0655) and from Cave-In Deathrite ordering (0692).

Burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic burrows every Deathrite minion at the chosen land site in canonical instance-id order, then pauses in deathrite-order before both die. Magic-resolved is deferred until the order is chosen. Distinct from Cave-In survivor order (0587) and from single-target Bury Deathrite settlement (0691).

Submerge-target-minion Magic offers a same-region minion at a Water site and forcefully submerges a minion without Submerge. After south summons at C1 on a Water site, casting Drown moves the minion underwater and it dies. Distinct from 0591, which keeps a Submerge minion in play.

Targetless healController Magic pays its cost with no target, restores the caster Avatar through the printed-life cap, and cannot leave Death's Door. Life stays at zero, the game stays active, and no healing event is emitted from Death's Door. Distinct from 0651–0652, which offer a chosen Avatar.

Leap-attack-ally Magic steps a controlled ally, then pauses in deathrite-order when that step settles two wounded Deathrite allies who lost a nearby power bonus. After either Deathrite order, the pending leap strike resumes at the destination and kills the enemy there. Distinct from ordinary Leap Attack (0599–0600), which never defers the strike.

A 1x1 caster stages Chain Magic through distinct nearby hops and damages every chosen unit simultaneously on resolve. Extra hops cost two mana, already-chosen units cannot be hopped again, and hops cannot leave the caster region. Distinct from oversized Spellcaster footprint hops (0385–0386).

Magic targets stay in the caster region. After a surface caster's ally is burrowed, that ally is no longer offered while an exposed surface enemy stays reachable. Distinct from 0673 (Fatality region filter) and from 0023 (Stealth exclusion).

Freeze Disable on an underground Burrowing minion immediately settles its region: the same receipt emits minion-disabled then minion-died, and the unit leaves play. Distinct from 0661–0662, which Freeze a surface minion until the next Start Phase or absorb into Ward, and from a surface Burrowing minion that stays in play after Disable.

Lash damage-then-untap Magic offers only a nearby minion, deals printed damage, and untaps the target only when it survives. A distant minion is not offered. Distinct from 0595, which has no nearby filter and does not untap.

grantPowerToAllyThisTurn Magic offers controlled allies, raises current derived power by +2 per source until the current End Phase, and feeds source-aware prevention. Stacked grants expire together before turn-ended. Distinct from 0529–0530, which grant to a minion then draw and do not offer Avatars.
Zero-domain site recovery offers every nearest empty cell in canonical order and rejects forged destinations. Distinct from ordinary expansion when the player still controls sites.
Zero-domain site recovery onto Rubble replaces the Rubble before the site is played. Distinct from 0701, which only enumerates nearest cells and rejects forgery.

Sinkhole sacrifices a source site, prevents destruction on protected targets, preserves existing Rubble, and still creates neutral Rubble on ordinary targets. Distinct from site_destruction_rules.rs 0012 replay, which omits subsurface occupants.

Sinkhole destruction on a Water site preserves relative subsurface: drowned minions die, Burrowing survivors and loose Artifacts settle underground, and terminal Atlas loss ends the game after Rubble. Distinct from 0703 land, protected, and existing-Rubble branches.

Craterize pays a mandatory Atlas discard, destroys an unprotected target site into Rubble, applies its full Manhattan damage grid across regions and statuses, and resolves deterministically. Distinct from 0657, which uses a flat 1-damage grid in Session replay.

Craterize refuses casts without an Atlas discard, rejects paying with the target site, and still damages occupants when the target site cannot be destroyed. Distinct from 0658 protected-site Session slice.

Raise Dead resolves an empty cemetery as a paid no-op, otherwise draws one public random minion from the combined cemetery pool before opening free placement. Distinct from 0583-0584 Session replay after a kill setup.

Raise Dead fails a 2x2 footprint summon when no legal location exists: the selected corpse stays in its cemetery, emits minion-summon-failed with no-legal-location, and the Magic still resolves. Distinct from 0707 empty-pool and free-placement branches.

A two-mana Chain Magic is not offered while the caster has only one mana. With a surface minion at C4 and a burrowing ally underground at C3, begin-chain-magic on the surface target is legal once mana is sufficient, but extend-chain-magic to the underground unit is illegal because hops cannot leave the caster region. Distinct from 0696 happy-path hops and simultaneous resolve.

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic burrows a chosen Burrowing Deathrite minion while two wounded allies share the site. The receipt emits magic-cast and minion-burrowed only, enters deathrite-order with magic-resolved deferred, and checkpoint create/resume preserves the pending state. After order-deathrites, both Deathrites draw sites, both minions die, and magic-resolved completes in main. Distinct from immediate single-target Deathrite settlement (0691) and Cave-In area ordering (0692).

Fight-ally-with-adjacent-enemy Magic may choose the casting player's Avatar as the ally; strike damage against the Avatar emits avatar-life-lost instead of minion damage. Distinct from 0603 minion ally.

Fight-ally-with-adjacent-enemy Magic in the underground region with a first-strike attacker pauses in deathrite-order after the initial strike when the target's Deathrite would settle. The pending continuation keeps the underground fight with first-strike semantics, defers magic-resolved until Deathrites are ordered, and checkpoint serialize/parse/resume preserves the pending state through terminal completion. Distinct from surface Duel proofs (0603–0604) and Leap Attack Deathrite resume (0695).

When a Water site floods the underground layer at a cell, underground minions relayer to underwater before state-based settlement runs. A Burrowing minion with deathrite-damage-each-unit-here still allocates damage to co-located units using its underwater source region, and surviving targets remain underwater with the allocated damage. Distinct from Sinkhole subsurface preservation on water destruction (0704) and ordered Deathrite deferral during Bury (0710).

Playing a Water site onto Rubble that floods underground Burrowing Deathrite minions emits rubble-replaced and site-played, enters deathrite-order with a site-genesis continuation carrying genesis-gain-mana, and leaves one mana from the site play. After order-deathrites on the canonical first source, both Deathrites draw sites, both minions die, mana-gained completes Genesis, and play returns to main with two mana total. Distinct from immediate single-target Deathrite settlement (0691) and Cave-In area ordering (0692).
When two 2×2 minions with overlapping footprints attack each other, declare-attack chooses the lowest shared contested cell.

Damage-each-unit-at-location-within-two-steps Magic measures connected surface locations from the caster footprint. With a partial B2–C4 site cluster, only connected cells within two steps are offered. Casting at C2 damages a 2×2 surface minion there but not a Burrowing minion at the same cell underground.

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic checks every cell of a 2×2 footprint for bury eligibility. Rubble counts as land, so a mixed land-and-rubble square still burrows and kills a non-Burrowing minion. Distinct from ordinary 1×1 Bury death (0655) and Burrowing survivor Bury (0585).

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact Magic still offers a 2×2 minion on an all-Water footprint, then resolves as a paid no-op because no Underground layer exists. The minion stays on the surface with its full footprint unchanged. Distinct from 1×1 Water no-op (0656) and mixed land-and-rubble oversized bury (0717).

A Geomancer Avatar with replace-adjacent-rubble-with-top-atlas-site and site genesis-heal-nearby-avatars on owner Atlas cards passes self-play admission whether the healing Genesis is on the same deck or an unrelated opponent Atlas card.

Granary Rats with siteProvidesNoThreshold ignores void and underground copies for suppression but keeps suppressing while any enabled copy occupies the site. A dual earth+fire site restores both affinities when every suppressor is voided, underground, or disabled.

Kill-target-wounded-minion Magic breaks Ward without killing the warded target. Healthy, enemy-stealthed, and underground wounded copies are filtered from targets; allied wounded minions remain legal even when stealthed. One proof combines Ward absorption with the healthy, Stealth, underground, and allied filter matrix. Distinct from 0609–0610 (wounded versus healthy), 0673–0674 (region only), and 0620 (unconditional kill Ward).
This-turn +2 power raises observed attack and defense for Avatars and disabled minions. Disabled, stealthed, and warded allies remain valid grantPowerToAllyThisTurn targets.
Sparkmage may activate at a nearby location that has rubble but no site.
Discard-here damage ignores disabled or removed sources and counts an oversized enemy footprint once in its hidden candidate pool. Extends 0154.
isTower + gainsPowerRangedAndSpellcasterAtopTower: occupant gets +2 power whether site controller is owner or enemy. Distinct from 0151, which proves the owned-Tower case.
End-turn Artifact life loss on a carried Artifact uses the oversized bearer's chosen cell for site controller attribution. Extends 0156.
End-turn cleanup resets both players' air-threshold cast counters to zero, not just the ending player. Extends 0149.
Pick Up and Drop ignore non-local Artifacts and disabled units. Extends 0140.

Alternate summon payment facts (random-card discard and local-minion sacrifice discount) are self-play safe, and random-card discard summons require an eligible hand card before issuing. Extends 0015–0016.

Burrow-target-minion-or-artifact and burrow-all-minions-and-artifacts-at-target-land-site Magic pass self-play admission when paired with ordinary minions, Burrowing, Submerge, Waterbound, Landbound, Voidwalk, start-turn and end-turn triggers, Deathrite library effects, forced-attack facts, and common Artifact bearer modifiers including composed Mask effects.
Post-action settlement tails slot before magic-resolved, so terminal game-ended follows magic completion rather than magic-cast.
Ordered terminal cleanup omits resolved Chain Magic from authoritative state instead of serializing pendingChainMagic as null.

Blink Magic passes self-play admission when paired with ordinary minions, Burrowing, Submerge, Waterbound, Landbound, Voidwalk, start-turn and end-turn triggers, Deathrite library effects, forced-attack facts, and common Artifact bearer modifiers including composed Mask effects.

Grant-charge, grant-first-strike, grant-ranged, grant-airborne, grant-power-two, grant-lethal, and grant-double-damage-next-strike Magic pass self-play admission when paired with ordinary minions, Burrowing, Submerge, Waterbound, Landbound, Voidwalk, start-turn and end-turn triggers, Deathrite library effects, and forced-attack facts on south-spell-1.

Gain-control-of-target-enemy-minion-this-turn, gain-control-of-target-enemy-minion-until-stealth-lost, and gain-control-of-target-nearby-minion Magic pass self-play admission when paired with ordinary minions, Burrowing, Submerge, Waterbound, Landbound, Voidwalk, start-turn and end-turn triggers, Deathrite library effects, forced-attack facts, and common Artifact bearer modifiers including composed Mask effects.

Every admitted Magic effect shape passes self-play manifest admission without unsupported-manifest rejection, including blink, burrow, submerge, control, grant, cemetery, and targeted-damage variants omitted from the earlier partial meta loop.
Geomancer terrain replacement ends the game terminal when the last Atlas card is played and skips deferred Genesis mana gain.
Opposing Lance-bearing minions in a Defend fight strike early simultaneously, break Lance in striker order, and apply damage before cleanup.
A Ranged Lance projectile breaks Ward then Lance, and power-threshold prevention uses unbuffed printed power rather than the Lance bonus.
Cave-In burrows a minion bearer underground while its carried Artifact remains attached instead of detaching like Avatar-carried Artifacts.
Missed Ranged shots and fixed-damage projectiles retain Lance without adding its strike bonus or breaking the mark.
Lance breaks before a lethal Deathrite draw that would deck out the controller, and terminal replay preserves that ordering.
Forward-only minions with top-bottom connection and movement bonus issue exact forward Defend paths without sideways or backward steps.
Attacking first strike snapshots every defender before a nearby disable-until-damaged aura awakens and changes strike allocations.
Simultaneous Genesis area damage snapshots each unit's status before a disable-until-damaged aura awakens and adds nearby power.
Disabled Stealth minions remain visible projectile targets, but a disable-until-damaged shooter cannot fire its fixed-damage projectile.
Fixed-damage projectiles classify prevention thresholds from the shooter's current power, not its printed attack.
Fixed-damage projectiles break Ward without dealing damage, kill through Lethal regardless of defense, and kill ordinary minions when damage exceeds defense.
Attacking first strike pauses on ordered Deathrites, lets each controller commit source order, then resumes normal return strikes exactly once.
A Stealthed minion keeps Stealth while joining Defend and loses it only when the fight interaction closes.
Siege Ballista activation requires a ready bearer tap plus a second ready ally at the same location; neither a tapped bearer nor a lone ready bearer suffices.
A disable-until-damaged bearer cannot pay Siege Ballista's first tap, so the carried Artifact offers no activation.
End-turn Artifact life loss charges the current site controller but skips Rubble, which has no controller.
End-turn Artifact life loss resolves before end-phase deaths drop the Artifact where its bearer fell.
End-turn ordered Deathrites pause the turn transition until every source order resolves, then resume turn-ended and turn-started.
Adjacent Updraft Ridge sites keep Airborne Defend path enumeration bounded to the free-departure routes.
A Disabled bearer skips its end-phase death, but a carried Artifact still charges the site controller at end turn.
A carried Artifact charges the surface site above an underwater bearer, not the void beneath subsurface regions.
Siege Ballista may target the ready ally that paid its second tap, killing that ally while the bearer still pays its tap.
A terminal end-turn Deathrite ends the game without emitting turn-ended or turn-started.
Payload Trebuchet discarding a Site pays zero damage to every unit at the target location and does not break Ward.
Payload Trebuchet area damage includes the origin cell where its bearer, helper, and Avatar stand, using the discarded card's mana cost as damage.
A Stealthed attacker loses Stealth only after undefended-site strike and life-loss events complete.
Simultaneous return damage above 255 aggregates the exact total on damage-dealt without u8 overflow.
A loose Lethal Artifact on a site does not grant Lethal to a minion fighting on that cell.
A minion with printed Stealth that is Disabled by Waterbound remains visible to enemy attack targeting.
Ranged projectile actions require an enabled ready minion; disable-until-damaged suppresses issuance.
An Airborne minion with cannotDefend is excluded from Updraft Ridge free-departure Defend paths.
A loose Lethal Artifact does not lend Lethal to adjacent-location area damage from a minion ability.
An Immobile Ranged minion with a post-strike step fact offers no optional step after firing.
Sideways-only movement restriction excludes every vertical Defend path while leaving other response actions unchanged.
Zero-power Avatars in combat allocate no strike damage and emit no zero-damage or zero life-loss events.
A finished avatar_defeated game replay exposes the winning and losing seats through Game::outcome().

A Ranged minion with mayRangedStrikeOnceDuringBasicMovement pauses incremental Move and Attack movement for one projectile shot mid-path, exhausts that strike, and resumes along the remaining path to activate move-and-attack.

A later-entered persistent 2×2 Flood Aura covering the same site wins the timestamp: the site becomes a Water site and provides Water threshold, while its other affinities remain. Drought entered first stays in the realm.
Simultaneous draw-site Deathrites resolve NAP then AP before minions enter their cemeteries; an empty Atlas skips those draws and finishes in a draw.
Movement +1 issues and applies an exact two-step Defend path, joining the attack and removing the original target.
Attacking-only first strike kills the defender before return damage while attacking, and is inactive while defending so equal minions trade simultaneously.
A minion with cannotDefend is excluded from movement Defend paths but may still Defend in place and Intercept when co-located.
Malakhim with untapsAtEndOfControllerTurn untaps at its controller End Phase only when tapped and not Disabled; ready minions skip untap and Disabled minions stay tapped while damage resets.

A ready minion with tap-to-shoot fixed projectile damage may fire in each direction, skip Stealth along the ray to the first visible unit, tap and lose Stealth while keeping Ward, and deal its fixed amount on hit.
End-turn Artifact life loss on a carried Artifact charges the site controller of the cell its bearer currently occupies, following the bearer when it walks to a new site.

Stacked end-turn Artifact life losses charge the site controller separately, can reduce life to zero and open Death's Door without ending the game, and further end-turn charges on Death's Door record triggers without reducing life.
Magic can destroy a realm Aura that sources an immobile area. The Aura moves to its owner's cemetery, the matching immobile area lifts, and the event is aura-destroyed rather than a duration dispel.
The Belfry untaps a nearby Avatar at end of turn even when no minion occupies the site.
Surviving minion damage persists through the turn and clears in End Phase.
Bladderblimp Deathrite makes each player lose life for their nearby sites.
Defend moves a unit into a simultaneous fight and stages exact split damage.
Ignited with diesAtEndOfControllerTurn dies at its controller End Phase before turn cleanup unless Disabled; Disabled Ignited minions survive cleanup while damage resets and disable effects expire.
Genesis sleep ends on real damage without retroactive strikes.
Oversized ground movement checks every newly entered terrain cell for legality.
A draw-spell Avatar pays its tap cost and keeps the drawn identity private.
Later undefended site strikes cannot deliver Death's Door death blows.
Deathrite damage preserves each source's power until resolution.
Takes-less prevention applies to each simultaneous damage source before Lethal.
Genesis draws a hidden site and an empty Atlas loses after summoning.
Immobile units attack and Defend in place but cannot move themselves.
Lance buffs and breaks on the next unit strike but not a site strike.
Leap Attack Deathrite order branches match after checkpoint resume.
Mountain Pass blocks only occupied ground-minion entry.
Mulligan returns chosen cards to the deck bottom in stable order.
Sparkmage may tap for zero damage at a nearby location with no other unit.
Deathrite healing caps at maximum, fails at Death's Door, and precedes cemetery entry.
A fully prohibited minion cannot use Defend or Intercept.
Declining an attack gives only co-located ready enemies an Intercept window.
An oversized ground minion manifest with Mountain Pass is admitted by the footprint core.
Mountain Pass blocks ground-minion entry when a friendly minion already occupies it.
A ground minion already on Mountain Pass may leave the occupied pass.
First player skips its draw, establishes a domain, then second player chooses a deck.
Sites expand through unoccupied orthogonal cells controlled by their player.
The Avatar may draw a private site instead of playing one.
Drawing a site from an empty Atlas pays the tap cost and loses.
Attempting to draw from an empty deck immediately loses.
